newsitem.title: GERMANY: Levy renews call for Syria to enter talks.
newsitem.headline: Levy renews call for Syria to enter talks.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy on Monday renewed an appeal to Syria to enter peace talks with no preconditions.
Levy told reporters in Bonn after meeting his German counterpart Klaus Kinkel that Israel remained committed to the principle of land-for-peace.
Syria demands that Israel agree to return the strategic Golan Heights as the price for talks to resume, but Levy said there should be no preconditions.
"We want to continue talks with Syria to bring peace to the region," he said. "That means any party can bring up any subject that contributes to peace."

"We don't prevent anyone putting any subject on the table when we negotiate," Levy said. Anyone who said they would only negotiate when all their conditions had been accepted was asking Israel to capitulate, he said.
"If we keep negotiating we will eventually get peace."
Kinkel said there was some concern in the world that the Middle East peace process was possibly being allowed to stagnate.
He said European Union foreign ministers had agreed at their weekend meeting "that the peace and reconciliation process must go on and that the world is waiting for a signal (that it will go on)".
Kinkel said there was no question of Germany or the European Union holding back financial or economic support to put pressure on Israel or the Palestinians to accelerate the process.
